Mohit Kumar Behara vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 25 October,
2024
Author: Parth Prateem Sahu 
Bench: Parth Prateem Sahu
 1/4 
 2024:CGHC:42396  NAFR  HIGH COURT OF CHHATTISGARH AT BILASPUR  WPS No. 6884 of 2024  1 - Mohit Kumar Behara S/o Shri Chandan Singh Behara Aged About 42  Years Presently Working On The Post Of Food Safety Officer In The Office  Of The Deputy Director, Food And Drug Administration, Bilaspur, District  Bilaspur Chhattisgarh, R/o Abhishek Vihar, Phase-Ii Quarter No. 152,
 Mangla, Bilaspur, District Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh  ---- Pet  versus  1 - State Of Chhattisgarh Through The Additional Chief Secretary,
 Department Of Health And Family Welfare, Mantralaya, Mahanadi Bhavan,
 Atal Nagar, Nava Raipur, District Raipur, Chhattisgarh  2 - Commissioner Food Safety, Food And Drug Administration, Indravati  Bhawan, Atal Nagar, Nava Raipur, District Raipur, Chhattisgarh  3 - Controller Food And Drug Administration, Indravati Bhawan, Atal Nagar  Nava Raipur, District Raipur, Chhattisgarh  4 - Deputy Secretary Department Of Health And Family Welfare, Government  Of Chhattisgarh, Mantralaya, Mahanadi Bhavan, Atal Nagar - 492 002, Nava  Raipur, District Raipur, Chhattisgarh  5 - Shri Nitesh Kumar Mishra Food Safety Officer Office Of Controller Of  Food Balrampur District , Balrampur  ---- Respond Mohit Kumar Behara vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178400724/
1 ____________________________________________________________ For Petitioner : Mr. Dhiraj Kumar Wankhede, Advocate For Respondents/State : Ms. Akanksha Verma Dabhadker, P.L. Hon'ble Shri Justice Parth Prateem Sahu Order On Board 25/10/2024 1. Petitioner has filed this petition seeking following relief (s) :-
"10.1 Call for the entire records leading to issuance of the impugned communication and impugned order Annexure P-1 for the kind perusal of this Hon'ble Court. 
10.2 Issue appropriate writ (s)/direction (s)/ order (s) quashing the impugned order dated 14.10.2024 Annexure P-1, qua the petitioner. 
10.3 Pass appropriate orders, in favour of the petitioner, so far as the cost of the litigation and other miscellaneous expenses are concerned.
10.4 Grant any such other relief in favour of petitioner as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit in the interest of justice." 
2. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that earlier petitioner vide order dated 30.09.2022 was transferred from Bilaspur to Bastar, which was challenged before this court and considering the grounds raised, interim protection was granted. Petitioner was again transferred by the impugned order dated 14.10.2024 and again he has been transferred to interior scheduled area Balrampur-Ramanujganj. He submits that transfer of petitioner is in the mids of academic session. 
Daughter of petitioner is student of Class - 10th and studying in Colonel's Academy of Radiant Education, Bilaspur. It is the base class of student to opt further extreme of studies to move forward in carrier. If petitioner is to shift at transferred place of posting, studies of her daughter will adversely be affected. He submits that in similar circumstances, Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Director of School Education, Madras & Ors. Vs. O. Karuppa Thevan & Anr, reported in 1994 Suppl.
(2) SCC 666 has observed that children of an employee who are studying should be given due weightage. He next contended that wife of petitioner is carrying pregnancy of about six months,
therefore, also, shifting of petitioner at this stage may adversely affect health of his wife.
Immediately after receipt of order of transfer, petitioner has already submitted representation before respondents on 18.10.2024, however, no decision has been taken on the same till the date. He also contended that petitioner till date has not been relieved from his present place of posting. 
3. Learned State counsel opposes the submission of learned counsel for petitioner, however, she submits that if representation of petitioner is still pending consideration, it will be considered and decided expeditiously. She has also not disputed the submission of learned counsel for petitioner with respect to reliving of petitioner from present place of posting. 
4. I have heard learned counsel for parties and perused the documents placed on record. 
5. Considering the submission of learned counsel for parties, nature of grievance raised in particular considering the fact that daughter of petitioner is student of Class -10 th and also the decision of Mohit Kumar Behara vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178400724/
2 Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Director of School Education, Madras & Ors. (Supra) this writ petition at this stage is disposed of directing respondents to take decision on the pending representation submitted by petitioner in accordance with law expeditiously preferably within period of three weeks from the date of receipt of this order. Petitioner is directed to submit copy of order within 10 days. 
6. Considering the fact that petitioner has not been relieved till date, til the decision on the representation submitted by petitioner, parties are directed to maintain status-quo as it exists today with respect to place of posting of petitioner. 
Sd/-
(Parth Prateem Sahu) Judge Balram Mohit Kumar Behara vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178400724/
